Abu al-ʻAlaʼ al-Maʻarri, The Luzumiyat, translated by Ameen Rihani.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/abu-al-ala-al-maarri/the-luzumiyat/ameen-rihani

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Abu al-ʻAlaʼ al-Maʻarri, the author, died 1057.
- Ameen Rihani, the annotator and translator and writer of accompanying material and writer of the preface, died 1940 (citizenship: Ottoman Syria).

First publication of the text used: 1920 (SE colophon: 'The Luzumiyat was published in the 11th century CE by Abu al-ʻAlaʼ al-Maʻarri. It was translated from Arabic in 1920 by Ameen Rihani.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1920, before 1931. A published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 2015.
- Country of origin (the country of first publication is not named in the facts; possible countries: United Kingdom, Ireland, United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India, South Africa): each of these countries has a term of life + 70 years or less. The last person to die did so in 1940, so the work is public domain in each of them from 1 January 2011.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook.
